marks.gloss_en: אלא מבלבלי; הכא נמי מבלבלי -- rather, they are intermingled; here too they are intermingled
rather, they are intermingled

מאי שנא טמאין מעיקרא דלא? דאמרינן איידי דמיא יקירי שכני תתאי... -- אי הכי, טהורים ולבסוף נטמאו נמי! -- the supposed reason would equally defeat contact for pure-then-impure water, which the baraita permits; unanswered, and the text concludes הכא נמי מבלבלי
since water is heavy it settles below and the fruit floats above, and the contact does not reach the water
temed, before it ferments -- one brings it into contact with water [to purify it]
Rav Yehuda (and likewise Rav Nachman): one says 'between holy and holy' in the blessing's conclusion
Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi: one says it even in the blessing's opening
מיתיבי: תוקעין ולא מריעין -- מאי לאו לא מריעין כלל? the baraita seems to forbid any terua, against Rav Yehuda's terua from within the tekia
לא, רב יהודה מתרץ לטעמיה: not a terua by itself, but from within the tekia (= p_ry_lo_meriin_bifnei_atzmah)
the same מיתיבי: if 'no terua' means none at all, it contradicts Rav Asi's tekia-and-terua in one breath
ורב אסי מתרץ לטעמיה: not in two breaths, but in one breath (= p_ra_lo_meriin_bishtei_neshimot)
the baraita: a Festival falling on Shabbat eve -- one sounds a tekia and does not sound a terua
Rav Yehuda: one sounds a tekia and sounds a terua from within the tekia
ולית הלכתא כוותיה -- the halakha is not as R' Dosa's formula 'between the more severe holiness and the lighter holiness'
and the halakha is not as he [R' Dosa] says
R' Dosa: [havdala of a Festival at the conclusion of Shabbat says] 'between the more severe holiness and the lighter holiness'
דתניא: the baraita names R' Meir as the one who says 'wherever there is sale there is no fine...' -- the mishna's own words -- and has the Sages differ
Rav: this [mishna] is the view of R' Meir
דתניא... וחכמים אומרים: from three years and one day until she matures she has a fine
the Sages: a minor girl from three years and one day until she matures has a fine
קנס -- אין, מכר -- לא? -- the Sages' clause names only a fine: does it mean she has a fine and no sale?
אימא: אף קנס במקום מכר -- read it: also a fine where there is sale
wherever there is sale there is no fine, and wherever there is a fine there is no sale
דתניא: until when does a girl refuse? until two hairs -- R' Meir; R' Yehuda: until the black exceeds the white
דתניא... רבי יהודה אומר: until the black exceeds the white -- adduced for 'there is refusal where there is chalitza'
Rav: this [mishna] is the view of R' Meir
wherever there is refusal there is no chalitza, and wherever there is chalitza there is no refusal
מאי טעמא? סדר הבדלות הוא מונה -- the reason for R' Zeira's formula: one is enumerating the series of distinctions

R' Zeira: a Festival that falls in the middle of the week -- one says 'who distinguishes between holy and profane, and between light and darkness, and between Israel and the nations, and between the seventh day and the six days of labour'
wherever there is a shofar blast, there is no havdala
a Festival falling on Shabbat eve: one sounds the shofar and does not say havdala
